title: Present Tense 1: First Conjugation Core
description: Russian splits its verbs into two big conjugation classes. Today we drill the first one: the -ю / -ешь / -ет / -ем / -ете / -ют endings on the cleanest verbs in the language.
descriptionRussian: Глаголы первого спряжения с окончаниями -ю / -ешь / -ет / -ем / -ете / -ют на чистых основах: читать, делать, работать, знать, понимать, гулять.
intro: A Russian verb ending does a job English hands to a pronoun: it carries who is acting. That is why the ending can never be dropped, and why reaching for the wrong one does not merely sound off, it points the sentence at the wrong person. Almost every verb in the language runs on one of two ending sets, so the whole system is smaller than it first looks. This lesson locks the first and larger set, on the cleanest verbs Russian has.
rules: Most first-conjugation verbs end in -ать or -ять in the infinitive. Drop -ть to get the stem; attach the six endings: -ю, -ешь, -ет, -ем, -ете, -ют. Other infinitives join this conjugation too (жить, пить, идти, ехать), which Lesson 7 takes up.
The я-form ends in -ю (читаю), the они-form ends in -ют (читают). They share the -ю sound but differ in the final -т.
Russian has no separate 'to be' in the present tense. 'Я гуляю' means both 'I walk' and 'I am walking', depending on context.
The вы-form (читаете) is used for formal singular 'you' and plural 'you'. Ты is informal singular only.
examples: Я читаю книгу. (I am reading a book.) Я + читаю: 1st-person singular ending -ю.
Ты делаешь домашнее задание? (Are you doing the homework?) Ты + делаешь: 2nd-person singular -ешь.
Антон работает в банке. (Anton works at a bank.) Он + работает: 3rd-person singular -ет.
Мы знаем ответ. (We know the answer.) Мы + знаем: 1st-person plural -ем.
Вы понимаете по-русски? (Do you understand Russian?) Вы + понимаете: 2nd-person plural / formal -ете.
Дети гуляют в парке. (The children are walking in the park.) Они + гуляют: 3rd-person plural -ют.

items.promptEnglish: I read a book every evening.
items.hint: Which subject is the sentence about? Match the ending to that person.
items.explanation: The subject is я (1st-person singular). The first-conjugation я-ending is -ю, attached to the stem чита-: читаю.

items.promptEnglish: Are you doing your homework right now?
items.hint: Ты forces a specific ending. The 2nd-person singular ending in this class is...?
items.explanation: The subject is ты (2nd-person singular informal). The first-conjugation ты-ending is -ешь, attached to the stem дела-: делаешь. Watch the -шь spelling: the soft sign at the end is required.

items.hint: Антон is one person, third person. Which ending matches that?
items.explanation: The subject Антон is 3rd-person singular (he). The first-conjugation 3sg ending is -ет, attached to the stem работа-: работает. Note that English 'works' and 'is working' both translate as работает; Russian does not distinguish them in the present.

items.promptEnglish: We know the answer to this question.
items.hint: Мы is 1st-person plural. Which ending fits?
items.explanation: The subject мы (we) takes the 1st-person plural ending -ем. Stem зна- plus -ем gives знаем.

items.hint: Вы can be formal singular OR plural. Both take the same ending.
items.explanation: Вы always takes the -ете ending in this class, whether it addresses one person formally or several people. Stem понима- plus -ете gives понимаете.

items.promptEnglish: The children are walking in the park.
items.hint: Дети is plural. Third-person plural ending in this class is...?
items.explanation: Дети (children) is 3rd-person plural (they). The first-conjugation 3pl ending is -ют, attached to the stem гуля-: гуляют.

blanks: Маша _____ музыку каждое утро. (Masha listens to music every morning.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Маша is 3rd-person singular (one person, she). The first-conjugation 3sg ending is -ет: stem слуша- plus -ет gives слушает.

errorCorrection.sentence: Мои друзья отдыхает на море летом.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: My friends vacation at the sea in the summer.
errorCorrection.explanation: The subject друзья (friends) is third-person plural, so the verb takes the first-conjugation 3pl ending -ют: отдыхают. Отдыхает is the 3sg ending -ет, which fits a single subject like 'друг' or 'Антон', not a plural one. Russian marks the subject through the verb ending, so a plural subject demands the plural ending.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Do you read a lot in the evenings?
errorCorrection.explanation: The subject ты (informal singular 'you') takes the first-conjugation 2sg ending -ешь: читаешь. The soft sign -шь is required. Читает is the 3sg ending -ет, used for он/она or a noun like 'Маша'. The ты-form always ends in -шь in the present tense.

errorCorrection.sentence: Мы покупают хлеб в этом магазине.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: We buy bread at this store.
errorCorrection.explanation: The subject мы (we) takes the first-conjugation 1pl ending -ем: покупаем. Покупают is the 3pl ending -ют, which needs a 'they' subject like 'они'.

minimalPairs.explanation: The subject Маша is 3rd-person singular: one person, she. The 3sg ending is -ет (знает). The 3pl ending -ют (знают) would require a plural subject like 'они' or 'студенты'.

minimalPairs.context: Каждый день мы _____ книги в библиотеке.
minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Every day we read books at the library.
minimalPairs.explanation: The subject is мы (we), so the 1pl ending -ем is required: читаем. Читают is the 3pl form (они), which would need 'они' or another 3pl noun as the subject.

reviewVocab.definition: conjugation (the system of verb endings that signals who is doing the action)
reviewVocab.example: В предложении 'я читаю' окончание -ю показывает первое спряжение.

reviewVocab.definition: first conjugation (the -ать / -ять class with the -ю / -ешь / -ет / -ем / -ете / -ют ending set)
reviewVocab.example: Глаголы 'читать', 'работать' и 'гулять' относятся к первому спряжению.

reviewVocab.definition: ending (the suffix that encodes person and number on a verb)
reviewVocab.example: В форме 'читаем' окончание -ем означает первое лицо множественного числа.
